scope: Supervisor handshake, lifecycle phases, control recovery, event waits and safe shared storage
changes: Bounded launch acknowledgement over a private Unix socket pair; durable recovery after a missing reply
Blocking owner-lock wait with a one-second client deadline; pending waiter retains launch admission lock
Rust lifecycle phase exposed through UniFFI, independent from host state and control reconnection
Rust client paces failures and retains the most recent observed snapshot during metadata or IPC failures
Blocking control accept with explicit shutdown wakeup and teardown fallback for removed socket
Generation-based event and EOF notification replaces the 250 ms runtime wait timer
Unique temporary file and rename shared by diagnostics and session metadata, with explicit file-fsync policy
Single runtime tree traversal validates ancestors before opening files and retains full SHA-256 verification
additional_coverage: IPC failure retains Running, Online, game identity and installation guards, then reconnects
Failed process-identity query does not imply process exit
Acknowledgement channel closed before reply does not abandon accepted launch
Native helper acknowledgement and preparation failure without loading Valve or contacting Steam
Owner-lock timeout blocks competing starters until owner release
Unreadable metadata does not regress an already observed live session
Removed control socket cannot block supervisor exit
Incomplete atomic writes retain previous file and clean temporary files
Equal-size, equal-mtime cache tampering is detected
Runtime root, file and nested-parent symlinks are rejected
Swift reconnection messaging preserves Running action and guards

validation_limits.protocol_compatibility: Existing serialized lifecycle phases and Observe/Cancel commands are unchanged; client reconnection status is not serialized.
